title: Aunt away, $10 short before payday, and a heavy first week of December before a flight

changes.content: My aunt is visiting family overseas from October 12 until November 22

changes.label: Her aunt is away, so nobody is cooking at home

dev_must_notice.what: After $85.17 at Target this afternoon, checking has $40.00 available. The phone bill ($30) and Claude ($20) come out Thursday, Nov 5, and pay lands Friday, Nov 6, so she comes up about $10 short on Thursday, before any coffee or lunch.

Since Oct 12 she spends about $45 a week more on food: the campus cafeteria went from about $5 to $20 a week, mostly Monday and Wednesday lunches, and fast food from about $35 to $65. It started the day her aunt left and should end when she is back on Nov 22.

Dec 1 to 8 holds five midterms (BIO Dec 2, MATH Dec 7 and CHEM Dec 8 in person; PSY and ENG online with open windows), her usual Tuesday and Saturday shifts, and about a week and a half of trip prep before the Dec 10 flight. Her schedule posts two weeks ahead, so the shifts for those weeks land around Nov 15 and Nov 22; until then those nights are unknown, not free.

best_fix.what: Tonight, after her shift: one message with the trace ($85.17 at Target, $40 left, $50 of bills Thursday, pay on Friday) and two taps: [Move $10 from savings] or [Remind me Thursday morning]. The move happens only if she taps it.
best_fix.why: One tap before Thursday avoids a $29 overdraft fee; after Friday's paycheck the gap is gone.

best_fix.what: Sunday at 2 PM, before her usual Sunday shop: one cheap meal-prep recipe from a cited source that packs for Monday and Wednesday lunches, a note that home is 10 minutes away on those long breaks, and a 45-minute prep block after the shop. Check back the next Sunday with the real change in food spending.
best_fix.why: The rise has a clear cause and an end date. A plan for the next three weeks fits her goal to cook more and saves about $30 a week without nagging.

placements.label: Meal prep for Monday and Wednesday lunches

best_fix.what: Flag it now with a plan built backwards from Dec 10: morning study before class in her usual 8 to 9:50 window and on Saturday mornings, both online exams early on rested mornings inside their windows, trip errands on a free Sunday afternoon and packing on the last evening, and a suggestion to ask her manager for lighter shifts Dec 1 to 9 before that schedule posts around Nov 22. Replan when each schedule lands.
best_fix.why: Five exams, two shifts a week and trip prep land in the same nine days. Asking for lighter shifts only works before the schedule posts, and her mornings are where she actually studies.

placements.label: BIO 110 last look before the 10 AM exam
Pack and check in for the flight

placements.note: No routine for cooking; it sits after her Sunday shop and before her call with Mom.
Her usual weekday morning slot, during Thanksgiving break.
A rested morning inside the exam window, not after a shift.
First morning of the window, so the weekend stays free for MATH and CHEM.
Before a Saturday shift, if one is posted.
After her kept-free Sunday morning, before her usual shop.
Packing is not study, so an evening is fine; classes are over for the term.

tempting.suggestion: put study blocks in her free weekday evenings
tempting.why_wrong: she studies mornings before class and never after 1 PM

tempting.suggestion: plan study on a Sunday morning
suggest a second workout on a day she already went at 7 AM
tempting.why_wrong: she goes Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 7, once

must_not: count Friday's paycheck as money she has
move money between her accounts on its own
treat the higher food spending as permanent (her aunt is back Nov 22)
comment on her weight, her body or what she eats
put study blocks in her free weekday evenings (she studies mornings only, never after 1 PM)
plan study on a Sunday morning (kept free)
schedule anything on Sunday evening (her call with Mom)
suggest a second workout on a day she already went at 7 AM
treat the unposted December shifts as free nights
assume a fixed number of study hours per exam
send all three messages on the same day
assumptions: The college's fall term ends Dec 9, with the second midterms from Dec 1 to Dec 8.
The grocery store posts schedules two weeks ahead, on Sunday afternoons.
A 9.5% tax share covers federal, state and FICA withholding on a part-time student job.
An overdraft costs $29 at her credit union.
Her aunt gets $150 on the 1st for groceries and utilities, and her parents send money by Zelle around the 1st.
